blogs.title: Why Finetuning Giant AI Models Is So Expensive—and How BOFT Cuts the Cost
blogs.description: This post introduces the big problem the paper tackles: adapting massive pretrained models without retraining billions of parameters. It explains parameter-efficient finetuning in plain language, compares common methods like LoRA, adapters, and prompt tuning, and shows how BOFT offers a new way to keep updates small while preserving model quality.

blogs.title: Orthogonal Finetuning, Explained: Teaching AI New Tricks Without Erasing What It Learned
blogs.description: This post focuses on the core intuition behind orthogonal finetuning. It explains how rotating a model’s internal weight space can preserve relationships between neurons, why that may help retain pretrained knowledge, and how BOFT builds on this idea to make orthogonal finetuning practical at larger scales.

blogs.title: From FFT to Foundation Models: How Butterfly Math Makes AI Finetuning Efficient
blogs.description: This post unpacks the paper’s most distinctive technical idea: butterfly factorization. It explains, with simple analogies, how a concept borrowed from the fast Fourier transform can build dense transformations from a sequence of sparse ones, reducing parameter counts from roughly quadratic to near-linear-logarithmic.

blogs.title: An Information Highway for Neural Networks: BOFT’s Clever View of Matrix Updates
blogs.description: This post centers on the paper’s ‘information transmission’ perspective. Instead of treating matrix factorization as abstract math, it explains it as routing information across a network of nodes. The article shows how this lens helps the authors design better sparse structures and why butterfly connections are more expressive than simple block-diagonal ones.

blogs.title: BOFT vs. LoRA: Two Different Philosophies for Lightweight AI Adaptation
blogs.description: This post compares BOFT with LoRA in accessible terms. It contrasts additive low-rank updates with multiplicative orthogonal updates, discusses differences in stability, expressiveness, and inductive bias, and helps readers understand when preserving a model’s geometry might be more useful than adding compact new weights.

blogs.title: One Finetuning Method for Vision, Language, and Diffusion? What BOFT’s Results Suggest
blogs.description: This post highlights the paper’s experimental significance. It explains how BOFT was tested across vision transformers, large language models, and text-to-image diffusion systems, and why that matters: the method appears to work as a general-purpose finetuning strategy rather than a niche trick for a single model family.
